title: Bounded failover window and circuit + fallback orchestra for sessioned streaming
creator: Marco Li
description: Introduce a coordinated failover choreography for hosted API edge gateways that bounds user-visible disruption during active-active region shifts. Focus: session- and stream-aware handoff, token-preserving KV cache reconciliation, circuit-based progressive drain, and deterministic load-shedding policies tied to SLO tiers.
background: Customer incidents show live streaming sessions experience token loss or reconnect storms during cross-region cutovers.
Existing failover patterns rely on unilateral drains or blunt traffic redirects which cause broken sessions, double-consumption, and SLO violations.
goals: Limit failed streaming requests during region cutovers to <0.05% of requests for P99 latency sensitive customers.
Provide a bounded failover window (<= 30s) for handoffs where client-visible reconnection is minimized.
Ensure fallbacks to lower-cost model variants or degraded modes rather than hard failures.
Make breakpoints observable: per-session handoff status, KV-sync lag, circuit state transitions.
non_goals: Full live-migration of in-flight model KV caches across regions (out of scope).
Requiring client SDK changes for basic compatibility; prefer transparent server-side handling.
acceptance_criteria: Canaries show no more than 0.05% increased 5xx during a controlled failover test for P99 SLO customers.
Session continuity tests show <= 1 reconnect per 1000 active streaming sessions during cutover.
Rollout toggle (feature flag) can be turned off with no residual routing rules within 10 minutes.
technical_design: We propose a 'bounded-window orchestra' with three coordinated phases: 1) Pre-cutover stabilize: lock routing key affinity and snapshot session metadata TTLs. 2) Circuited drain: per-edge circuit breaker gradually increases 'drain intensity' based on interior metrics (queue length, GPU busy, KV-lag) with token-preserving redirects for stream resumes. 3) Reconciliation sweep: eventual async KV delta sync + per-session resume tokens stored in durable cross-region store (short TTL). Key elements: epoched session IDs, handshake on resume (client provides resume-token + epoch), ephemeral session proxy in egress region to stitch stream logs, and fallback routing to pre-configured model-variant in saturations. Circuits open/close thresholds are dynamic: open if 95th queue-latency > 2x target AND node-cpu>85% OR active-streams>N where N from p99 historical. Load-shedding implements tiered policies: P0 customers get soft-degrade (lower-context-length variant) before hard-drop; unrecognized callers are probed and then shed gradually by sampling 25/50/75%.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged canary in us-west-2 (5% traffic) for 48h with synthetic sessions.
Increase to 20% and run two scheduled cross-region cutovers with telemetry capture.
If canaries green, promote to 100% with staged ramp and monitoring playbook.
Fallback: revert flag + immediate soft-redirect to pre-cutover region for all active edges.
monitoring_and_alerting: New SLO metrics: session_handoff_success_rate, session_resume_latency, kv_lag_ms_percentile, circuit_open_count.
Dashboards: per-region per-edge heatmaps and a 'handoff runway' showing active sessions that will be affected by a cutover.
Alerts: paging when handoff_success_rate < 99.95% for 5m for P0 customers; warn if kv_lag_ms P99 > 500ms.
testing_plan: Unit tests for handshake protocol state machine and epoch validation.
Integration tests: simulated multi-region cutover harness with 10k synthetic streaming sessions validating token resume correctness.
Chaos tests: randomized failpoints (network partitions, delayed KV writes) in staging, asserting bounded window and no data duplication.
Load tests to validate dynamic circuit thresholds and load-shedding sampling behaviour.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Li: Initial design spike completed. Prototype handshake tokens looked feasible with current KV TTLs; need small API to persist resume-token to cross-region durable store.
2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Reviewed circuit thresholds; suggested adding historical-percentile-based adaptive thresholds rather than fixed constants. Assigned to Marco to implement metrics model.
2026-03-07 Evan Morris: Raised concern about passporting tokens across legal boundaries for Private customers — flagged to Security for review (SEC-579).
2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Implemented feature-flag gating and local canary runner. First 1k-session smoke tests passed; observed kv_lag_ms P99=160ms under light load.

2026-03-11 QA Team: Integration harness revealed a race where resume handshake could be accepted by both old and new edge when TTLs overlap; mitigation: add monotonic epoch numbers and single-writer resume-token claim.
2026-03-12 Marco Li: Updated design to include monotonic epochs and single-writer claim; writing PR for edge-gateway (see links).
